Sebuleni Pro Max AI - Software Requirements Specification

This SRS defines the v1 requirements for an OHLC-based predictive assistant that learns from one selected instrument at a time, uses an active multi-timeframe stack of 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and 1d, derives higher timeframes from 1-minute bars, predicts absolute price move events regardless of direction, and provides grounded explanations without executing trades.

Requirements validation result

The requirements are now complete enough to produce a design-grade SRS, a complete system architecture, and a detailed implementation roadmap without blocking ambiguity. The remaining variable elements are configuration values, not missing requirements.

Requirement area Resolved decision
Input data 1-minute OHLC only, with user-configurable source timezone.
Modeled timeframes The active timeframe stack is 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and 1d. Timeframes above 1m are deterministically resampled from the 1-minute source.
Execution scope One selected instrument per training, validation, test, and live deployment cycle.
Event type Absolute move magnitude regardless of direction.
Reference price Latest close of the latest fully closed bar.
Event start First future bar where excursion first crosses the user-defined price-difference threshold.
Maturity Point of maximum excursion within the prediction horizon.
Boundary meaning Lowest and highest reachable prices within the horizon.
Inference input Only fully closed 1-minute bars may be used in live inference.
Validation standard Rolling walk-forward validation.
User surfaces REST API, CLI, and batch report generation.
Deployment target Single machine hosting all v1 services.
Learning lifecycle Offline training, live inference, and controlled retraining with manual plus scheduled review.

Project overview

Sebuleni Pro Max AI is a single-user predictive intelligence system for financial OHLC time-series analysis. It consumes 1-minute OHLC data for one chosen instrument, builds and models the timeframe stack 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and 1d, learns multi-timeframe price behavior, detects event precursors, predicts reachable price boundaries and event timing, estimates confidence, and explains outputs using historical analogs.

The system does not place trades, execute orders, optimize entries, or manage positions. Its sole responsibility is to provide predictive and interpretive outputs that may support downstream human decision-making.

Objectives

  1. Learn regime-sensitive OHLC price behavior for one instrument at a time.
  2. Predict whether absolute price excursion from the latest closed bar will exceed a user-defined threshold within one or more horizons.
  3. Estimate lowest and highest reachable prices within each forecast horizon.
  4. Estimate event start, maturity, and duration inside the horizon.
  5. Produce calibrated confidence and low-confidence advisory outputs when evidence is weak.
  6. Provide explanation grounded in top-K historical analogs, summary statistics, and deterministic natural-language rationale.
  7. Support reproducible training, walk-forward evaluation, live inference, and controlled retraining on a single machine.

Scope

In scope

  • 1-minute OHLC ingestion and deterministic preprocessing.
  • Active multi-timeframe modeling across 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and 1d.
  • User-configurable deterministic resampling from 1m into 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and 1d.
  • Calendar and session-aware processing with user-configurable timezone, weekend policy, holiday policy, and source-data timezone.
  • Feature engineering from OHLC and calendar/time context, including deterministic derived price-action features.
  • Walk-forward training and validation.
  • Prediction of event probability, confidence, reachable boundaries, event start, maturity, duration, and explanation.
  • REST API, CLI, and batch report generation.
  • Single-machine deployment with local persistence, logging, and scheduled jobs.
  • Manual and scheduled retraining workflows.

Out of scope

  • Trade execution, broker integration, order routing, or risk management automation.
  • Cross-instrument joint training in v1.
  • Distributed training or cloud-native production infrastructure.
  • Real-time inference on incomplete bars.
  • Unbounded online self-adaptation without review.
  • Multi-user authentication and role-based access control beyond single-user local operation.
  • Dashboard UI in v1.

User roles

v1 supports a single physical user role.

Role Description Capabilities
System Operator The sole user who configures instruments, runs training, requests predictions, generates reports, reviews metrics, and triggers retraining. Manage configuration, execute CLI commands, call API endpoints, run scheduled jobs, inspect logs, approve retraining, and review reports.

Functional requirements

ID Requirement
FR-1 The system shall ingest 1-minute OHLC data for one selected instrument at a time from a user-provided source.
FR-2 The system shall validate input schema, timestamp order, duplicates, missing bars, timezone configuration, and instrument/session configuration before training or inference.
FR-3 The system shall deterministically resample the 1-minute stream into 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and 1d bars using OHLC-consistent aggregation rules.
FR-4 The system shall support user-configurable source-data timezone, runtime timezone, weekend handling policy, holiday handling policy, DST-aware session handling, and a daily close definition of 5:00 PM New York time.
FR-5 The system shall generate deterministic features from OHLC data and calendar/time context. Feature generation may include derived price-action features such as returns, ranges, and wick/body ratios.
FR-6 The system shall generate self-supervised labels where an event occurs if future highest high or future lowest low produces an absolute excursion from the latest closed-bar close that crosses the user-defined price-difference threshold within the selected horizon.
FR-7 The system shall define event start as the first future bar where the threshold-crossing excursion occurs.
FR-8 The system shall define maturity as the point of maximum excursion within the prediction horizon.
FR-9 The system shall support both single-horizon prediction per run and multi-horizon prediction using a configuration-driven fixed horizon list.
FR-10 The system shall train using chronological rolling walk-forward validation and shall never use future information in preprocessing, labeling, feature generation, or evaluation.
FR-11 The system shall learn multi-timeframe latent representations across the active stack of 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and 1d using a shared backbone and specialized prediction heads.
FR-12 The system shall produce event probability, confidence, lowest reachable price, highest reachable price, event start estimate, maturity estimate, duration estimate, and explanation outputs.
FR-13 The system shall produce low-confidence advisory output instead of hard refusal when analog support is weak, confidence is low, or recent data is imperfect but still processable.
FR-14 The system shall provide top-K analogs, summary statistics, and a short deterministic grounded natural-language explanation for each prediction.
FR-15 The system shall expose prediction and management capabilities through a REST API.
FR-16 The system shall expose training, inference, evaluation, reporting, and retraining workflows through a CLI.
FR-17 The system shall support batch report generation for offline analysis runs and scheduled reporting workflows.
FR-18 The system shall support manual retraining and scheduled retraining jobs, with metric-based alerts used to recommend review rather than auto-promote new models.
FR-19 The system shall log all failures, warnings, degraded-mode outputs, retraining decisions, and inference anomalies in structured form.
FR-20 The system shall fail early on malformed inputs, invalid configuration, missing files, invalid dtypes, invalid dimensions, or timestamp misalignment.

Non-functional requirements

  • All preprocessing shall be deterministic and reproducible.
  • Random seeds shall be configurable.
  • The system shall support CPU execution and shall detect CUDA gracefully when available.
  • The system shall avoid non-deterministic algorithms unless explicitly enabled.
  • Training, validation, test, and inference shall remain isolated.
  • All public inputs shall be validated with meaningful exceptions.
  • Configuration shall live in YAML, JSON, TOML, or environment variables rather than hardcoded constants.
  • The v1 production target is single-machine deployment.
  • Inference latency shall satisfy the acceptance thresholds defined in this SRS.
  • No silent drops, silent data repairs, or silent timestamp corrections are allowed.

Data model

Core entities

Entity Key fields Description
InstrumentConfig instrument_id, source_timezone, runtime_timezone, weekend_policy, holiday_policy, session_calendar, daily_close_time All market and calendar rules for the selected instrument.
MinuteBar timestamp, open, high, low, close Validated input 1-minute OHLC row.
ResampledBar timeframe, start_ts, end_ts, open, high, low, close Derived OHLC bar for 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, or 1d. The 1m frame remains the base and also participates directly in modeling.
FeatureWindow reference_ts, timeframe_windows, calendar_features, derived_features Multi-timeframe model input anchored to a closed reference bar.
EventLabel reference_ts, horizon_bars, threshold, event_flag, event_start_offset, maturity_offset, future_low, future_high Self-supervised target record derived from future excursion.
ModelArtifact model_id, instrument_id, training_range, config_hash, artifact_path, metrics Versioned model and evaluation metadata.
PredictionRecord request_id, reference_ts, horizon, event_probability, confidence, low_price, high_price, start_estimate, maturity_estimate, duration_estimate Prediction output payload.
AnalogRecord analog_id, reference_ts, distance, outcome_summary Retrieved historical analog used for explanation.
AuditLogEntry timestamp, level, event_type, message, context Structured operational log.

APIs and interfaces

REST API

Endpoint Method Purpose
/health GET Return service health and model availability.
/predict POST Run single-horizon or multi-horizon inference on recent closed OHLC history.
/models/current GET Return currently loaded model metadata.
/reports/generate POST Generate a batch report for a configured range or dataset slice.
/retraining/request POST Create a retraining request for manual or scheduled workflow processing.

Prediction request contract

  • instrument_id
  • bars_1m: fully closed 1-minute OHLC bars only
  • horizon_mode: single or multi
  • horizon_bars when single-horizon mode is used
  • threshold: required price-difference threshold
  • top_k_analogs: configurable positive integer

Prediction response contract

  • event probability
  • confidence score
  • lowest reachable price
  • highest reachable price
  • event start estimate
  • maturity estimate
  • duration estimate
  • low-confidence advisory flag
  • top-K analogs
  • summary statistics
  • grounded natural-language explanation

CLI workflows

  • train
  • evaluate
  • predict
  • generate-report
  • request-retraining
  • inspect-model

Security considerations

  • v1 assumes single-user local or single-machine operation; full multi-user auth is out of scope.
  • All public inputs shall be validated and rejected on schema or type violations.
  • Services should default to local binding unless explicitly configured otherwise.
  • Configuration files must not contain credentials in plain text where avoidable.
  • Model artifacts, reports, and logs must be versioned and traceable to config and data ranges.
  • No hidden use of future data, silent data repair, or silent fallback behavior is allowed.

Error handling

  • Missing file, malformed bar, invalid dtype, duplicate timestamp, unresolved timezone, invalid horizon, and invalid threshold shall all fail early.
  • Prediction may return low-confidence advisory output when evidence is weak but input remains processable.
  • Incomplete recent bars shall be rejected for live inference rather than used speculatively.
  • All exceptions exposed through API or CLI shall include actionable diagnostics.

Logging

  • Structured logs shall be emitted for preprocessing, resampling, feature generation, training, evaluation, inference, reporting, and retraining requests.
  • All failures shall be categorized and reproducible.
  • No silent drops are permitted.
  • Every model run shall log configuration hash, instrument, date range, walk-forward fold identifier, metrics, and artifact locations.
  • Every inference request shall log request ID, reference timestamp, horizon mode, threshold, latency, degraded-mode flag, and model version.

Configuration

All mutable system behavior shall be configuration-driven. At minimum, configuration must cover:

  • instrument identifier and data source paths
  • source-data timezone and runtime timezone
  • session calendar definitions and daily close time
  • weekend and holiday policies
  • resampling targets
  • feature toggles and deterministic derived feature set
  • event thresholds and horizon configuration list
  • walk-forward fold settings
  • training hyperparameters and random seed
  • top-K analog count
  • API host/port and report output settings
  • scheduled retraining and reporting schedules

Testing strategy

  • Unit tests for resampling, timezone handling, session segmentation, feature engineering, labeling, model interfaces, explanation summarization, and API request validation.
  • Walk-forward evaluation tests that verify strict temporal isolation.
  • Integration tests from OHLC ingestion to prediction output.
  • Regression tests for deterministic identical-input identical-output behavior in explanation generation.
  • Performance tests for API latency, batch throughput, and feature computation cost.
  • Failure-mode tests for malformed input, missing bars, weak analog support, and invalid configuration.

Deployment strategy

v1 shall deploy all production services on a single machine, which may also be the development laptop configured in a server role. This machine shall host inference services, scheduled training and retraining review pipelines, batch reporting, local artifact storage, logging, and database services where applicable.

No cloud infrastructure, separate staging cluster, distributed workers, or multi-node deployment is required for v1. The deployment shall be restartable, locally reproducible, and operable by a single user.

Risks and assumptions

Assumptions

  • Historical 1-minute OHLC data is available in sufficient quantity and quality for one selected instrument.
  • Session definitions can be supplied by configuration.
  • Top-K analog retrieval remains computationally tractable on a single machine.
  • Single-user operation is acceptable for v1.

Risks

  • Session and timezone misconfiguration may silently distort bar semantics unless strictly validated.
  • Label noise may rise if event thresholds are too loose or horizons are too wide.
  • Cross-timeframe leakage risk is high if resampling and alignment are not strictly causal.
  • Explanation credibility may degrade if analog support is weak during unusual regimes.
  • Single-machine deployment may face resource contention during scheduled training and live inference if not managed.

Acceptance criteria

Category Threshold
Event precision >= 0.85
Event recall >= 0.80
Event F1 >= 0.82
False positive rate <= 15%
Performance drop across folds <= 10%
Expected Calibration Error <= 0.04
Brier score <= 0.12
Reliability curve deviation +/- 5% per bin
Boundary coverage / valid processing rate >= 99%
Ambiguous or unresolved samples <= 1%
Silent drops 0
Timestamp misalignment errors 0
API latency <= 100 ms target, <= 50 ms preferred, p95 <= 150 ms
Batch inference <= 2 s per 10,000 samples
Feature computation <= 300 ms per 1,000 candles
Latency spike policy No spike > 2x median without logging alert
Explanation consistency >= 90%
Explanation human-verifiable alignment >= 85%
Explanation contradiction rate <= 10%
Unexplained high-confidence predictions 0 when p > 0.75
Walk-forward performance variance <= 8% to 10%
Worst fold floor >= 0.70 of median performance
This SRS is intended to be sufficient for another senior engineer to implement v1 without ambiguity, subject to approval before implementation begins.
